correctness.rationale: The five source equations at \(r=1\) give a one-dimensional center direction. Direct invariance-equation matching uniquely determines the displayed Taylor coefficients through the quintic term. Substitution is checked symbolically in verify.py. originality.rationale: The exact quintic coefficient and induced logarithmic correction were not present in the same-model sources inspected. The closest paper already contains the cubic first-transition normal form, so the accepted claim is explicitly narrowed to the next center-manifold order and its long-time consequence. published-finding corpus and the existing ledger returned no same-model equivalent or stronger statement.
residual_risks: A generic pitchfork theorem plus the previously published cubic coefficient already yields the leading \(t^{-1/2}\) scale; originality is claimed only for the explicit quintic coefficient and resulting logarithmic term.
Unindexed or unpublished derivations could exist; failed search is not treated as a proof of universal novelty.
Center manifolds are nonunique beyond flat terms, although the finite Taylor jet used here is fixed by the invariance equations to the displayed order.

value.rationale: The calculation is attached to the model’s distinguished first Rayleigh transition and sharpens the known cubic normal form by the first subleading long-time invariant. It reveals that the added-mode damping \(d\), central to the model’s stability interpretation, is invisible in the leading critical relaxation but enters its first logarithmic correction. This is a natural structural refinement rather than an arbitrary slice or table recomputation.
